issues.description: Inconsistent getter naming for the StockIngredient 'name' field across artifacts: the template defines the getter as getIngredientName() (and Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getIngredientName()), while the solution uses getName() (and its Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getName()). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not standardize the getter name. This API/name mismatch between template and solution can confuse students when they compare their implementation with the reference solution or when they rely on sample code, as they may not know which getter name is intended.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the getter name for the StockIngredient 'name' field across all artifacts. Prefer using getName() (to match Meal.getName()) and update the template files accordingly: rename getIngredientName() to getName() in template StockIngredient.java and ensure template Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getName(). Alternatively, keep getIngredientName() and update the solution to use getIngredientName() everywhere. Also update the problem statement to explicitly state the expected getter naming convention to avoid ambiguity.

issues.description: The getter for the StockIngredient name is named inconsistently across artifacts: the template's StockIngredient class exposes getIngredientName(), while the solution uses getName(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not mandate getter names; nonetheless, students will reasonably expect the conventional getName() getter. This mismatch (getIngredientName vs getName) can create unnecessary mapping confusion when students read the template, the UML in the problem statement, and the solution, and when they try to follow or implement Stock.findStockIngredient and other code that uses the name getter.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the getter name for the StockIngredient name field across all artifacts. Prefer the conventional name getName(): (a) rename template's getIngredientName() to getName() and update all usages (e.g., Stock.findStockIngredient) to call getName(); or (b) if keeping getIngredientName(), update the solution and all references to use getIngredientName(). Align documentation/UML to mention the chosen getter name so students have a single, consistent target.
